review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

1:1.sourceText: Ἀποκάλυψις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἣν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεός, δεῖξαι τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει, καὶ ἐσήμανεν ἀποστείλας διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου αὐτοῦ, τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ Ἰωάνῃ,
1:1.targetText: This is the revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants what must soon come to pass. He made it known by sending His angel to His servant John,

groups.note: ἐν τάχει ("in quickness") together mean soon.
σημαίνω ("make known, signify") is rendered made … known.
The participle ἀποστείλας ("having sent") gives the means of making known, rendered by sending.
The dative δούλῳ supplies to.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
BSB makes the angel the one sent, so διά ("through") has no English word (as Matthew 11:2).

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a presentational frame; the Greek title has no verb.
English supplies the object.

1:2.sourceText: ὃς ἐμαρτύρησεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅσα εἶδεν.
1:2.targetText: who testifies to everything he saw. This is the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ.

groups.note: The aorist ἐμαρτύρησεν is rendered with an English present.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB puts the objects of ἐμαρτύρησεν in a separate sentence and supplies This is.

1:3.sourceText: Μακάριος ὁ ἀναγινώσκων καὶ οἱ ἀκούοντες τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας καὶ τηροῦντες τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ γεγραμμένα· ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς ἐγγύς.
1:3.targetText: Blessed is the one who reads aloud the words of this prophecy, and blessed are those who hear and obey what is written in it, because the time is near.

groups.note: The one Μακάριος covers both groups; BSB repeats blessed for the second.
The article τῆς is rendered this.
The participle τηροῦντες ("keeping") shares the article οἱ with ἀκούοντες.
The article with the participle γεγραμμένα ("the things written") is rendered what is written.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.
English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.
English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.

1:4.sourceText: Ἰωάνης ταῖς ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαις ταῖς ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἑπτὰ Πνευμάτων ἃ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου αὐτοῦ,
1:4.targetText: John,  To the seven churches in the province of Asia:  Grace and peace to you from Him who is and was and is to come, and from the seven Spirits before His throne,

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The dative ἐκκλησίαις supplies To.
After ἀπό the Greek keeps this title in the nominative; the article with the participle ὤν ("the one who is") is rendered Him who is.
The article with the finite verb ἦν works as a title ("the one who was") under the same Him who.
The article with the participle ἐρχόμενος ("the one coming") is rendered is to come.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative ἅ ("which are") without an English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds that Asia was a Roman province.

1:5.sourceText: καὶ ἀπὸ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ μάρτυς ὁ πιστός, ὁ πρωτότοκος τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ ὁ ἄρχων τῶν βασιλέων τῆς γῆς. Τῷ ἀγαπῶντι ἡμᾶς καὶ λύσαντι ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ αἵματι αὐτοῦ,
1:5.targetText: and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth.  To Him who loves us and has released us from our sins by His blood,

groups.note: The titles stand in the nominative after the genitive Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
The genitive νεκρῶν ("of the dead") is rendered from … dead.
The article with the participle ἀγαπῶντι ("the one loving") is rendered To Him who loves.
The participle λύσαντι shares the article Τῷ with ἀγαπῶντι.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated article of the adjective πιστός has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:6.sourceText: καὶ ἐποίησεν ἡμᾶς βασιλείαν, ἱερεῖς τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ αὐτοῦ, αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
1:6.targetText: who has made us to be a kingdom, priests to His God and Father—to Him be the glory and power forever and ever! Amen.

groups.note: BSB turns καί with the finite verb ἐποίησεν ("and he made") into a relative clause; the verb's subject is rendered who.
The dative Θεῷ supplies to.
The genitive τῶν αἰώνων ("of the ages") completes the idiom forever and ever; there is no separate Greek and.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the clause as "who has made", so καί has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies to be with the second object of ἐποίησεν; the Greek has no verb here.
English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.

1:7.sourceText: Ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται μετὰ τῶν νεφελῶν, καὶ ὄψεται αὐτὸν πᾶς ὀφθαλμὸς καὶ οἵτινες αὐτὸν ἐξεκέντησαν, καὶ κόψονται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς. ναί, ἀμήν.
1:7.targetText: Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him—even those who pierced Him. And all the tribes of the earth will mourn because of Him. So shall it be! Amen.

groups.note: ναί ("yes") is rendered as the affirmation So shall it be.

1:8.sourceText: Ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ, λέγει Κύριος ὁ Θεός, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, ὁ Παντοκράτωρ.
1:8.targetText: “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, who is and was and is to come—the Almighty.

groups.note: Ὦ is the letter omega.
The article belongs to Θεός; BSB places its the before Lord God.
The article with the participle ὤν ("the one who is") is rendered who is.
The article with the finite verb ἦν works as a title ("the one who was").
The article with the participle ἐρχόμενος ("the one coming") is rendered is to come.

1:9.sourceText: Ἐγὼ Ἰωάνης, ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὑμῶν καὶ συνκοινωνὸς ἐν τῇ θλίψει καὶ βασιλείᾳ καὶ ὑπομονῇ ἐν Ἰησοῦ, ἐγενόμην ἐν τῇ νήσῳ τῇ καλουμένῃ Πάτμῳ διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ.
1:9.targetText: I, John, your brother and partner in the tribulation and kingdom and perseverance that are in Jesus, was on the island of Patmos because of the word of God and my testimony about Jesus.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The article τήν is rendered my.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB gives the place as the island of Patmos, leaving τῇ καλουμένῃ ("the one called") without an English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English turns the phrase ἐν Ἰησοῦ ("in Jesus") into a relative clause.
English joins the name to island with of; the Greek name stands in apposition.

1:10.sourceText: ἐγενόμην ἐν Πνεύματι ἐν τῇ κυριακῇ ἡμέρᾳ, καὶ ἤκουσα ὀπίσω μου φωνὴν μεγάλην ὡς σάλπιγγος
1:10.targetText: On the Lord’s day I was in the Spirit, and I heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet,

groups.note: The adjective κυριακῇ ("belonging to the Lord") is rendered Lord’s.

1:11.sourceText: λεγούσης Ὃ βλέπεις γράψον εἰς βιβλίον καὶ πέμψον ταῖς ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαις, εἰς Ἔφεσον καὶ εἰς Σμύρναν καὶ εἰς Πέργαμον καὶ εἰς Θυάτειρα καὶ εἰς Σάρδεις καὶ εἰς Φιλαδελφίαν καὶ εἰς Λαοδικίαν.
1:11.targetText: saying, “Write on a scroll what you see and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.”

groups.note: The dative ἐκκλησίαις supplies to.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists the cities with commas, without and between them.
BSB does not repeat to before each city in the list.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object.

1:12.sourceText: Καὶ ἐπέστρεψα βλέπειν τὴν φωνὴν ἥτις ἐλάλει μετ’ ἐμοῦ· καὶ ἐπιστρέψας εἶδον ἑπτὰ λυχνίας χρυσᾶς,
1:12.targetText: Then I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me. And having turned, I saw seven golden lampstands,

1:13.sourceText: καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τῶν λυχνιῶν ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, ἐνδεδυμένον ποδήρη καὶ περιεζωσμένον πρὸς τοῖς μαστοῖς ζώνην χρυσᾶν·
1:13.targetText: and among the lampstands was One like the Son of Man, dressed in a long robe, with a golden sash around His chest.

groups.note: ἐν μέσῳ ("in the middle of") together mean among.
The accusative ὅμοιον continues the object of I saw in 1:12.
ποδήρη ("reaching to the feet") is used as a noun for the robe.
The participle περιεζωσμένον ("girded") is rendered as a with phrase.
πρός ("at") marks where the sash is worn.
The article τοῖς is rendered His.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB joins the two descriptions with a comma, so καί has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and verb; the Greek continues the object of the verb in 1:12.

1:14.sourceText: ἡ δὲ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ αἱ τρίχες λευκαὶ ὡς ἔριον λευκόν ὡς χιών, καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ὡς φλὸξ πυρός,
1:14.targetText: The hair of His head was white like wool, as white as snow, and His eyes were like a blazing fire.

groups.note: In the Greek λευκόν describes the wool; BSB uses it for the comparison with snow.
ὡς ("like") is rendered by the comparison as … as.
The noun φλόξ ("flame") is rendered by the adjective blazing.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB turns "His head and hair" into "the hair of His head", so καί has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins hair and head with of; the Greek joins them with καί.
English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.
English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.

1:15.sourceText: καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὅμοιοι χαλκολιβάνῳ ὡς ἐν καμίνῳ πεπυρωμένης, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ αὐτοῦ ὡς φωνὴ ὑδάτων πολλῶν,
1:15.targetText: His feet were like polished bronze refined in a furnace, and His voice was like the roar of many waters.

groups.note: The participle πεπυρωμένης is genitive in the Greek; BSB uses refined for the bronze.
The second φωνή ("sound") is rendered the roar.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ὡς ("as") before in a furnace without an English word.

1:16.sourceText: καὶ ἔχων ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ ἀστέρας ἑπτά, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ῥομφαία δίστομος ὀξεῖα ἐκπορευομένη, καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος φαίνει ἐν τῇ δυνάμει αὐτοῦ.
1:16.targetText: He held in His right hand seven stars, and a sharp double-edged sword came from His mouth. His face was like the sun shining at its brightest.

groups.note: The participle ἔχων ("holding") is rendered as a finite verb.
The participle ἐκπορευομένη ("coming out") is rendered as a finite verb.
The finite verb φαίνει ("shines") is rendered shining.
δυνάμει ("strength") is rendered brightest.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle ἔχων.
English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.

1:17.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε εἶδον αὐτόν, ἔπεσα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ὡς νεκρός· καὶ ἔθηκεν τὴν δεξιὰν αὐτοῦ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ λέγων Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος
1:17.targetText: When I saw Him, I fell at His feet like a dead man. But He placed His right hand on me and said, “Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last,

groups.note: δεξιάν ("right") stands for the right hand.

unmappedSource.reason: An opening καί linking to the previous verse is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle λέγων to the main verb with and; the Greek has no καί here.

1:18.sourceText: καὶ ὁ Ζῶν, καὶ ἐγενόμην νεκρὸς καὶ ἰδοὺ ζῶν εἰμι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, καὶ ἔχω τὰς κλεῖς τοῦ θανάτου καὶ τοῦ Ἅιδου.
1:18.targetText: the Living One. I was dead, and behold, now I am alive forever and ever! And I hold the keys of Death and of Hades.

groups.note: The article with the participle ζῶν ("the one living") is rendered the Living One.
The genitive τῶν αἰώνων ("of the ages") completes the idiom forever and ever; there is no separate Greek and.

1:19.sourceText: γράψον οὖν ἃ εἶδες καὶ ἃ εἰσὶν καὶ ἃ μέλλει γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα.
1:19.targetText: Therefore write down the things you have seen, and the things that are, and the things that will happen after this.

groups.note: μέλλει ("is about to") is rendered will.
The plural ταῦτα ("these things") is rendered this.

1:20.sourceText: τὸ μυστήριον τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀστέρων οὓς εἶδες ἐπὶ τῆς δεξιᾶς μου, καὶ τὰς ἑπτὰ λυχνίας τὰς χρυσᾶς· οἱ ἑπτὰ ἀστέρες ἄγγελοι τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησιῶν εἰσίν, καὶ αἱ λυχνίαι αἱ ἑπτὰ ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαι εἰσίν.
1:20.targetText: This is the mystery of the seven stars you saw in My right hand and of the seven golden lampstands: The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.

groups.note: δεξιᾶς ("right") stands for the right hand.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the relative οὕς ("which") without an English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB gives one the for the lampstands; it goes with the article before ἑπτά.

English makes the lampstands a second of phrase; λυχνίας is accusative in the Greek.
